impacts.text: Measured land subsidence in Jakarta ranged from about 1 to 15 centimetres a year, and up to 20 to 28 centimetres in a few places.
impacts.src: Abidin et al. (2011), Land subsidence of Jakarta (Indonesia) and its relation with urban development, Natural Hazards 59

impacts.text: Typical subsidence rates of 3 to 10 centimetres a year; several coastal areas now flood at high tide, mostly where the ground sinks fastest.
impacts.src: Abidin et al. (2015), On correlation between urban development, land subsidence and flooding phenomena in Jakarta, PIAHS 370

profile.text: A 2022 law makes Nusantara, on Borneo, the new capital, but Jakarta remains the capital until the President signs the decree on the move, as the Constitutional Court confirmed in May 2026.

impacts.text: At the 2021 census, 393 of Majuro’s 3,896 households said a king tide had hit their community in the past ten years, and 401 a storm surge.
impacts.src: RMI 2021 Census Report Vol. 1 (EPPSO & SPC, 2023), Table A17

impacts.text: Majuro’s land covers only 9.7 km², around a lagoon of about 295 km²; most of its people live on the eastern islets of Delap, Uliga and Djarrit.
impacts.src: World Bank, RMI Urban Resilience Project, PAD4708 (2022)

impacts.text: Modelling commissioned by the World Bank (Deltares and Tonkin & Taylor, 2021) shows that a storm expected once in ten years, at today’s sea level, can flood 67% of the land of Majuro’s urban strip, from Delap-Uliga-Djarrit to Rairok, to depths of 0.5 metres.
impacts.src: World Bank, RMI Urban Resilience Project, PAD4708 (2022), para 5 and footnote 7

profile.unit: m above local mean sea level
profile.text: Its land is a thin ring of islets around a lagoon, and half of it lies less than 1.9 m above local mean sea level.
profile.src: USGS 1 m terrain model of Majuro (Palaseanu-Lovejoy et al. 2017), our calculation

profile.text: At the 2021 census, 23,156 people lived on Majuro, the capital atoll: more than half of the Marshall Islands’ 42,418.

storms.name: Hurricane Sandy
storms.src: NOAA CO-OPS water level (6-min) and datums, station 8518750

impacts.text: Relative sea level at the Battery has risen about 3 mm a year (1.16 inches per decade) since 1856.
impacts.src: NOAA CO-OPS sea level trends station 8518750

impacts.text: IPCC AR6 finds it likely that the global proportion of major (Category 3–5) tropical cyclones has increased over the last four decades.
impacts.src: IPCC AR6 WGI SPM A.3.4

impacts.text: Sandy killed 44 people in New York City, displaced 35,000 residents and caused $19 billion in damage and lost economic activity.
impacts.src: NYC Mayor's Office of Climate and Environmental Justice, 'Sandy 10 Years Later' (Oct 2022), p. 3

impacts.text: Sandy flooded 51 square miles of New York City, 17 % of its land area, with nearly 90,000 buildings in the inundation zone.
impacts.src: NYC Mayor's Office of Climate and Environmental Justice, 'Sandy 10 Years Later' (Oct 2022), p. 3

impacts.text: Human-caused sea-level rise added about $8.1bn ($4.7–14bn) to Sandy’s damage across New York, New Jersey and Connecticut, about 13% of it, including about $1.5bn in New York City, and brought the flood to about 71,000 (40,000–131,000) more people.

profile.text: About 400,000 New Yorkers lived in the 1%-annual-chance floodplain on FEMA’s 2015 preliminary flood maps, more than then lived in Cleveland, Tampa or St. Louis.
profile.src: NYC Planning, Flood Risk in NYC (info brief, November 2016)

profile.text: New York City had an estimated 8.6 million residents in 2025.
profile.src: NYC Department of City Planning, Population Estimates and Trends, March 2026 (Census Bureau Vintage 2025)

defences.name: Public flood defence line
defences.basis: Design water level 7.30 m NHN at St. Pauli (before 2012); raised to 8.10 m NHN in 2012
defences.status: built; being raised by at least 0.80 m to about 2050
defences.src: LSBG Bericht Nr. 7, Hochwasserschutz in Hamburg - Anleitung Deichverteidigung, 2nd ed. 2015, p. 4

impacts.text: The February 1962 storm flood killed 315 people in Hamburg and flooded one sixth of the city; St. Pauli peaked at 5.70 m NN.
impacts.src: Freie und Hansestadt Hamburg BUKEA Sturmflut-Chronik

impacts.text: Hamburg raised its design water level from 7.30 to 8.10 m NHN; its public flood defences are to be raised by at least 80 cm over the coming 25 years.
impacts.src: LSBG Bericht Nr. 7 (2nd ed. 2015), p. 4 (design levels); BUKEA, Ellerholz project page (80 cm)

impacts.text: About 45 percent of Hamburg's area lies in storm-flood-prone lowland behind roughly 100 km of defences.
impacts.src: Freie und Hansestadt Hamburg BUKEA (Ellerholz project page)

impacts.text: The highest storm surge ever measured in Hamburg reached 6.45 m NHN at St. Pauli on 3 January 1976.
impacts.src: Freie und Hansestadt Hamburg Katastrophenschutz FAQ

profile.text: 1.87 million people lived in Hamburg at the end of 2025.
Its port handled 8.3 million TEU (standard container units) in 2025.
profile.src: Hafen Hamburg Marketing, throughput figures 2025 (19 Feb 2026)

name: Mekong Delta: Ben Tre and Tra Vinh

defences.name: Ba Lai dam (Ben Tre)
defences.datum: design crest elevation; datum not stated (the designer's tide charts use the Mũi Nai–Hà Tiên height system)
defences.status: built (2002); earth dam 544 m across the river, beside the sluice
defences.src: Trần Thanh Sơn (HEC-2, the designers), Notes on the design and construction of the Ba Lai dam, VNCOLD, about 2011, p. 2

impacts.text: The 2020 salinity intrusion potentially damaged about 30,000 hectares of rice in Ca Mau.
impacts.src: Park et al. (2022), Ambio 51

impacts.text: By 7 March 2020 five Mekong Delta provinces had declared a state of emergency over drought and saltwater intrusion affecting all 13 delta provinces.
impacts.src: UN Viet Nam Flash Update No. 3 (25 Mar 2020)

impacts.text: In the 2019–20 dry season, drought and saltwater intrusion left about 95,600 households short of water, and 38,800 ha of rice had been lost by 7 March 2020.
impacts.src: UN Viet Nam Flash Update No. 3 (25 Mar 2020), citing MARD

impacts.text: More than half of the Mekong Delta’s shoreline, over 600 km long, was eroding between 2003 and 2012.
impacts.src: Anthony et al. (2015), Scientific Reports 5

impacts.text: A model estimates that groundwater pumping alone made the Mekong Delta sink by about 1.1 centimetres a year on average around 2015, and by more than 2.5 centimetres a year in places.
impacts.src: Minderhoud et al. (2017), Environmental Research Letters 12

profile.text: Since July 2025, Ben Tre and Tra Vinh belong to the merged province of Vinh Long, home to 4.3 million people.
profile.src: National Assembly of Viet Nam, Resolution 202/2025/QH15, Art. 1(20)

profile.text: The Mekong Delta grows more than half of Viet Nam's rice and supplies about 90% of its rice exports.
profile.src: Nguyen, Ha-Tran & Huang 2025, Frontiers in Plant Science 16:1635193, section 2.1

impacts.text: Cyclone Aila killed 190 people in Bangladesh in May 2009, according to the Disaster Management Bureau.
impacts.src: Gupta 2009, Natural Hazards Center quick response report, p. 7, citing Bangladesh Disaster Management Bureau (2009)

impacts.text: Cyclone Amphan triggered about 2.5 million displacements in Bangladesh in 2020, mostly pre-emptive evacuations, the highest number recorded since 2008.
impacts.src: IDMC (2026), Disaster displacement risk in Bangladesh, p. 8

impacts.text: Disasters caused 21.2 million displacements in Bangladesh from 2008 to 2024, 11.3 million of them from cyclones and storm surges; these include pre-emptive evacuations.
impacts.src: IDMC (2026), Disaster displacement risk in Bangladesh, pp. 8-9, Fig. 2

impacts.text: Salt-affected land in coastal Bangladesh grew from about 0.83 million hectares in 1973 to 1.06 million hectares in 2009, by the soil institute's maps.
impacts.src: Soil Resource Development Institute (SRDI) maps 1973, 2000 and 2009, presented by Arifunnahar (SRDI), FAO Global Symposium on Salt-Affected Soils 2021, slide 3

profile.text: Shyamnagar, the subdistrict that includes the island of Gabura, had 366,000 people at the 2022 census.
profile.src: Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics, Census 2022, via citypopulation.de

profile.text: Next to it lies the Sundarbans, one of the largest mangrove forests in the world; three wildlife sanctuaries in its Bangladeshi part, about 140,000 ha, have been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1997.
profile.src: IUCN World Heritage Outlook, The Sundarbans (2025)

impacts.text: More than 280 buildings along Alexandria’s shoreline collapsed fully or partly between 2001 and 2021; the study links the collapses to coastal erosion and seawater intrusion, and counts more than 7,000 buildings at risk.
impacts.src: Fouad, Heggy et al. (2025), Earth's Future 13

impacts.text: With 0.44 m of sea-level rise plus measured subsidence a bathtub model puts 2660 km² of the northern delta below sea level by 2100 (defences not modelled).
impacts.src: Gebremichael et al. 2018 JGR Solid Earth doi:10.1002/2017JB015084

impacts.text: Radar measurements show the northern Nile Delta sinking 2.4 mm a year on average (2004–2010), and up to 9.7 mm a year over the Abu Madi gas field and where groundwater is pumped hardest in the southern and western delta.
impacts.src: Gebremichael et al. 2018 JGR Solid Earth doi:10.1002/2017JB015084

impacts.text: Before the seawalls were built in 1989–1990, the tip of the Rosetta promontory retreated about 137 m a year.
impacts.src: Ghoneim, Mashaly & Gamble, GSA Annual Meeting 2013, abstract 232988; published as Ghoneim et al. 2015, Geomorphology 228:1-14

profile.text: About half of Egypt's people live in or near the Nile Delta.
Alexandria, Egypt's second city, had about 5.5 million people in 2023.
Two seawalls armoured with concrete dolos units, 1.5 km and 3.35 km long, were built on either side of the Rosetta mouth in 1989–1990; we found no documented crest height for them.
profile.src: Ismail, Iskander & El-Sayed 2012, Coastal Engineering Proceedings (ICCE 2012), p. 6

profile.text: Lake Nasser, behind the Aswan High Dam, traps about 98% of the Nile's sediment: below the dam, the river carried 124 million tonnes a year before it and 2.5 million after.
profile.src: Makary, El-Moattassem & Fahmy 2004, Evaluation of Lake Nasser Environmental Sedimentation (1964-2000), Proc. 9th Int. Symp. on River Sedimentation (IAHR)

defences.name: Larose to Golden Meadow ring levee (Lafourche)
defences.datum: “above sea level” per the levee district; datum not stated
defences.src: South Lafourche Levee District (listing on LouisianaLandCAN, updated Sep 2022)

impacts.text: The island shrank from more than 22,000 acres to about 320 acres.
impacts.src: Louisiana Office of Community Development, Isle de Jean Charles Resettlement

impacts.text: Coastal Louisiana lost about 4833 km² of land between 1932 and 2016, about 25% of its 1932 land area.
impacts.src: Couvillion et al. 2017 USGS SIM 3381 doi:10.3133/sim3381

impacts.text: The rate of land loss peaked at about 83.5 km² a year in the mid-1970s and has slowed to about 28 km² a year.
impacts.src: Couvillion et al. 2017 USGS SIM 3381 doi:10.3133/sim3381

impacts.text: Coastal Louisiana's land surface is sinking on average 9 ± 1 mm a year based on 274 CRMS monitoring sites.
impacts.src: Nienhuis et al. 2017 GSA Today 27(9) doi:10.1130/GSATG337GW.1

impacts.text: With $48 million from HUD, residents began moving to The New Isle near Schriever in August 2022; 37 households had moved by autumn 2024.
impacts.src: Louisiana Office of Community Development, Isle de Jean Charles Resettlement

profile.text: On the USGS trend to 2016, coastal Louisiana loses wetland the size of an American football field about every 100 minutes.
Terrebonne and Lafourche parishes, home to Houma, Golden Meadow and Port Fourchon, had 207,000 residents at the 2020 census.
